newsitem.title: UK: ICI suffer after results, downbeat outlook.
newsitem.headline: ICI suffer after results, downbeat outlook.

text.p: Imperial Chemical Industries Plc saw its shares slip 21-1/2 pence to 903-1/2 by 0825 GMT, after its results statement offered little for investors to look forward to, said some analysts.
First half profits fell to 160 million stg from 367 million last year, as expected. ICI blamed the pound's strength and a continued collapse in bulk chemical prices.
Paul Diggle, analyst at SocGen, said "People expected ICI to say this. But maybe they are refining their numbers a little, division by division."

"Perhaps there is nothing in the statement to hang a second half improvement on. The statement is not encouraging one to feel the underlying business is making progress," even when the impact of sterling is stripped out, said Diggle.
Alan Spall, chief financial officer at ICI, told Reuters in an interview there was evidence the pound was hurting exports and hitting its UK customer base.
The pound has rocketed by 35 percent since last August and is now trading comfortably above three marks.
ICI said it would be happier with sterling in the 2.50 to 2.60 mark range.
Its comments mirror those of other major exporters like British Steel Plc, which has also seen its profits decimated by the level of sterling.
